skill.name: video-extend
skill.description: Continue existing Veo video clips through the RunComfy CLI using standard or Fast Extend endpoints and prompts describing the next action.
skill.summary: Extend Veo clips and chain narrative beats with RunComfy.
skill.author: prime-skills

security_audit.summary: All 52 static findings concern Markdown formatting, documented service links, standard credential storage, or endpoint recommendations rather than demonstrated malicious behavior. One semantic issue concerns misleading shell-safety guidance: JSON serialization alone does not safely quote arbitrary prompts for the illustrated Bash commands. No evidence found of credential exfiltration or instructions attempting to override the audit.

remediation.issue: Unversioned installation commands resolve a mutable CLI package release.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a pinned CLI version from a verified package source, and review the package before installation.

remediation.issue: The shell-safety claim overlooks Bash parsing before the CLI receives JSON, including apostrophes in prompts or URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Serialize JSON and pass it through a subprocess argument array without a shell. If Bash is required, use proper shell-argument escaping and test apostrophes.

semantic_findings.title: Incomplete Shell-Quoting Safety Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The claim "No shell-injection surface" overlooks Bash parsing before the CLI receives JSON. Directly inserting prompts containing apostrophes into the illustrated single-quoted argument could terminate quoting and enable command injection.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples use single-quoted JSON without shell-escaping guidance, while the safety claim relies on CLI behavior after shell parsing. Exploitability depends on agent substitution behavior.

content.value_statement: Short video clips often end before a scene or narrative is complete. This skill sends an existing clip and a continuation prompt to Veo through RunComfy, then returns the next segment.
actual_capabilities: Extends an existing Veo video with a prompt describing the next action.
Chooses standard Veo Extend or Fast Extend for quality and speed needs.
Supports chained extensions for multi-shot narratives.
Passes a source video URL and continuation prompt to the RunComfy CLI.
Downloads generated clips to a selected output directory.
Provides guidance for camera continuity, scene beats, and identity consistency.
limitations: It requires a reachable source video URL and a configured RunComfy account.
It does not create a first clip from text or an image.
Long chains can accumulate identity drift and visual inconsistencies.
It does not guarantee audio synchronization or exact scene continuity.

use_cases.title: Finish a Short Scene
use_cases.description: Extend an existing Veo clip so a camera move, character action, or visual beat reaches a complete ending.

use_cases.title: Build a Shot-by-Shot Story
use_cases.description: Chain short extensions to turn one seed clip into a longer narrative with planned beats and consistent visual direction.

use_cases.title: Prototype Video Variations
use_cases.description: Use Fast Extend for lower-cost drafts, compare continuation prompts, and reserve standard Extend for final delivery.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Scene Extension
prompt_templates.prompt: Extend this video by 4 seconds. Continue the existing motion naturally, keep the same subject and lighting, and describe only what happens next: [next action].
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner continuation of one simple action.

prompt_templates.title: Camera-Controlled Extension
prompt_templates.prompt: Continue the existing scene for 4 seconds. The camera [camera movement], while [subject action]. Preserve the current framing, lighting, environment, and subject identity.
prompt_templates.scenario: A controlled camera move with one main beat.

prompt_templates.title: Narrative Beat Extension
prompt_templates.prompt: Extend the previous shot for 5 seconds. Beat: [single story beat]. Keep the established visual style and physics. End with [clear transition state] for the next shot.
prompt_templates.scenario: A planned story beat in a chained sequence.

prompt_templates.title: Production Chain Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a continuation plan for this source clip. Propose three separate 3 to 5 second extensions, each with one action, camera anchors, and continuity constraints. Identify where a new image-to-video anchor may be needed.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a longer multi-shot sequence.

output_examples.input: An 8-second clip shows a cyclist approaching a bridge at sunrise. Continue the shot for 4 seconds.
output_examples.output: A continuation plan that keeps the sunrise lighting and camera direction, then has the cyclist begin crossing the bridge.

output_examples.input: Use Fast Extend to prototype the next story beat after a character opens a workshop door.
output: Endpoint choice: Fast Extend for draft iteration.
Continuation prompt: The camera follows behind as the character steps into the workshop and reaches toward a lit workbench.
Continuity note: Keep the doorway framing, warm interior light, and character identity.

best_practices: Describe only the next action because the source clip already establishes identity, lighting, and physics.
Use one primary story beat per extension and keep chained segments short.
Use source URLs that the user provided and review generated output for drift or unexpected behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not restate an entire scene when requesting a continuation.
Do not combine several unrelated actions in one extension prompt.
Do not use this skill when the task needs image-to-video creation, video restyling, or synchronized avatar speech.

faq.question: What input does this skill need?
faq.answer: It needs a reachable source video URL and a prompt describing the next visual action.

faq.question: Which Veo endpoint should I use?
faq.answer: Use standard Extend for final quality and Fast Extend for quicker, lower-cost iteration.

faq.question: Can I create a long video from one short clip?
faq.answer: Yes. Chain several short extensions, but inspect each result because identity drift can accumulate.

faq.question: Does it generate the first video clip?
faq.answer: No. Use an image-to-video or text-to-video workflow to create the initial clip.

faq.question: Can it preserve dialogue audio?
faq.answer: The skill does not guarantee audio synchronization. Use a dedicated avatar or audio workflow when timing is essential.

faq.question: How should I handle sensitive source footage?
faq.answer: Use only approved URLs, obtain user consent, and avoid uploading confidential footage to a remote model service.
